definition: Of or pertaining to a leap year; containing the intercalated day that keeps the calendar aligned with the solar year.
etymology: From Latin bissextilis, meaning the doubled sixth day. The Romans inserted an extra day by repeating the sixth day before the Kalends of March — counting it twice, bis sextus, twice-sixth. Julius Caesar embedded this correction into his reformed calendar, and the word has carried that arithmetical ghost ever since.
usage: June 30 falls at the exact midpoint of a bissextile year, meaning 2024 has already banked its extra February day and now coasts toward a second half with 184 days rather than the usual 183 — a quiet asymmetry most people never notice.
